Gusto’s cross from the right is put behind by Konsa for a Chelsea corner out on the right. Neto clips it in but Arsenal head away. James then opts to shoot from range and his effort is blocked by Gabriel. That shot looked to be going on target but Raya may have had it covered anyway.

Rice’s corner from the left is flicked on by Havertz at the near post and the last touch comes off James for another Arsenal corner on the other side. Arsenal take it short and fell to get into the danger zone but do win themselves another corner.

Saka delivers it into a dangerous area and the ball is flicked, looking like it is going into the Chelsea net, but Martinez makes the save whilst on the ground.

Havertz plays a first-time flick into the path of Saka, whose first-time effort looking for the far corner is saved well by Martinez to his right.

Odegaard feeds a clever pass into the Chelsea penalty area to pick out Zubimendi, whose shot is blocked.

Double change for Arsenal as Zubimendi and Hincapie replace Lewis-Skelly and Calafiori.

Palmer gets a shot away from the right side of the box but it is straight at Raya. Chelsea are just starting to wrestle back some momentum.

Gusto has only just come on but has a chance. The ball is laid to him on the edge of the box and he hits it first time but his effort goes over the bar.

The momentum is certainly with Arsenal right now so Xabi Alonso is making a double change. Gusto and Chavarria replace Lavia and Hato. With Gusto coming on for Lavia, Chelsea do not actually have any out-and-out central midfielders on the pitch.

Tzolis is the first Arsenal player into the book today. He is brought down by Lacroix and then demands that the Chelsea defender be booked, waving an imaginary card, and is then shown a yellow himself. Lacroix was also booked for the original foul.

Two former teammates challenge each other as Konsa slides in to make a perfectly-timed challenge on Rogers. The home crowd loved that tackle from Konsa, who won that tackle fair and square.

Chelsea made Odegaard angry about two minutes before that goal. The Arsenal captain, who is a mild-mannered guy, was really unhappy with a tackle by James. They were exchanging some verbals afterwards, before Odegaard then ran away from James to score.

That’s five goals Chelsea have conceded in just over a game-and-a-half since Emi Martinez took over in goal. In fairness, that Odegaard goal wasn’t his fault.

Arsenal were forced to respond when Chelsea scored early but now it is on the visitors to see how they respond after falling behind.

For the first time this afternoon, Arsenal lead and it is a quality goal. Tzolis receives it out on the left and cuts inside onto his right. Not even two minutes into the game, Chelsea take the lead and it is a man Arsenal wanted over the summer who scores against them. Bukayo Saka has arrived at a career crossroads. We will soon learn whether he is destined to be a good Arsenal player or if he will elevate himself to the level of Premier League, Champions League and England great.

This weekend Saka turns 25, an age when footballers typically enter their peak. Although his legendary status at Arsenal is secure as a title winner, the reaction to the champions’ transfer window suggests there is a general feeling that he can and should produce more to earn “world class” status.

Mikel Arteta is short of such an attacker. He spent the summer investigating whether players of Vinícius Júnior and Julián Alvarez’s calibre might add much-needed stardust to his front three. Failure to secure a big-name forward has led many to conclude that Arsenal’s title defence will be in the mould of their impressive, but cautious 1-0 victory at Aston Villa.

It is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

It is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

“This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once said of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. But you know how you always push your ‘little friends’ at that age? Well, we tried, but he was a competitive monster.”

A personal opinion that no one asked for: Arsenal should have signed Joao Pedro last summer, when the Brazilian joined Chelsea for £60m. Arsenal bought Viktor Gyokeres instead, in a deal that could ultimately be more expensive, and there is no doubt which forward offers more to their team. Joao Pedro always seemed to cause problems for Arsenal’s defence when he played against them during his time at Brighton, and he has a flexibility and versatility that would have been perfect for Arteta’s system. Arsenal had twice explored the possibility of signing him over the years. It is surely a source of regret that they never became serious about it. Today:Everton 0 Manchester United 0 HTArsenal vs Chelsea 4.30pm

Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

The departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

“We are better equipped,” said Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”

Asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very important to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”

Two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

“Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta said. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”

Chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

“In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso said. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, big and small.

“We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of big personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”

Arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.

Team news from the Emirates to follow shortly.

#1520. Manchester United targeting Dominic Calvert-Lewin in surprise January transfer move

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Manchester United could be forced to strengthen their attacking options in January after another injury setback involving Benjamin Sesko.

With Michael Carrick needing additional firepower to maintain competition for places up front, an experienced Premier League striker has reportedly emerged as a surprise target.

Leeds United forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin is among the names being considered by United’s recruitment team. However, attempting to sign a key player from one of their biggest rivals could prove extremely difficult.

According to The Athletic, Manchester United are exploring the January market for centre-forwards, with Calvert-Lewin one of the players under consideration.

The 29-year-old England international has reportedly been on United’s radar for some time, and recruitment staff are now assessing whether a potential transfer would be feasible when the window opens.

The interest comes amid concerns over Benjamin Sesko’s availability. The Slovenian striker is expected to miss an extended period with a shin injury, leaving Carrick with fewer recognised centre-forward options.

Calvert-Lewin has rebuilt his career since joining Leeds on a free transfer from Everton in 2025. His performances at Elland Road have attracted renewed attention, with the striker scoring 20 goals in 49 appearances for the club across all competitions.

He has also returned to England international contention following his improved form, making him an appealing option for United as they consider their attacking requirements.

However, there are significant obstacles. Leeds are reportedly keen to reward Calvert-Lewin with a new contract, despite his current agreement running until 2028. The club are also understood to be protective of a player who has become an important part of Daniel Farke’s side.

The rivalry between Leeds and Manchester United presents another major complication. A transfer between the clubs would attract considerable attention, and reports suggest the possibility of an agreement is currently remote.

Calvert-Lewin could offer United a different profile in attack, bringing physical presence, aerial ability and considerable Premier League experience. His availability could become particularly important if Sesko remains sidelined into the January window.

United have previously considered alternative centre-forward options, but the latest developments could encourage the recruitment department to widen its search. Calvert-Lewin’s experience in English football would potentially make him an attractive short-term solution.

Nevertheless, Leeds are unlikely to make negotiations straightforward. They have little reason to weaken their squad midway through the campaign, particularly by allowing an important player to join their historic rivals.

United must also consider whether pursuing Calvert-Lewin is realistic when other striker targets may be easier to acquire.

For now, the reported interest represents an option under consideration rather than an imminent transfer. Sesko’s injury has increased the urgency surrounding United’s search for attacking reinforcements, but persuading Leeds to sell their striker could prove a significant challenge.

#1519. GdS: ‘Turbo Milan’ – how Frosinone were dismantled by five-star counter-attacking display

AC Milan put in one of their best performances under Ruben Amorim so far to sweep aside Frosinone at San Siro.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report by writing that Lazio, Roma and Juventus also had fun this weekend, scoring a flurry of goals in their victories, but it is Milan that might just come away from the round 12 feeling best.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Within 20 minutes, the Rossoneri had already blown the game wide open, eventually putting five past their opponents. All of them were spectacular, lightning-fast, and following the same pattern: every single one a counter-attack.

It was a throwback style of football, yet infused with the visionary approach of Amorim, making it both fresh and truly beautiful to watch. There may not be official statistics on this, but conceding from five lethal transitions feels like a record as Frosinone’s strategy certainly went beyond mere self-sabotage.

Yet, on days like this, this Milan – an enigma to its opponents, with fluid movement and interchangeable positioning – are a truly daunting prospect. When Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Luka Modrić and others perform at such a high level, we see the potential of this side.

The Diavolo have secured five wins in their last six league matches, yet in Europe, they have suffered three defeats in four games. Will Thursday’s clash against Olympiacos help restore the balance?

There was nothing balanced about the game between Milan and Frosinone. It is true that Alvini’s incredibly bold (perhaps even reckless) side tried to go toe-to-toe with their opponents for an hour by attacking, playing long balls, and taking on defenders.

Yet, beyond this emphasis on a specific style of play, one could make more concrete assessments. The coach clearly understood how vital Raimondo is to a team featuring such direct and creative wingers, Ghedjemis on the right and Kvernadze (who was rather ineffective yesterday) on the left.

Raimondo was the perfect focal point for them and without him, things had already gone poorly against Cagliari. Alvini attempted to make adjustments but got it wrong: he abandoned his 4-2-3-1 formation in favour of a back three (Calvani, Monterisi, Cittadini).

All this was undermined by a senseless tendency to push too high, maintaining a defensive line 57 metres from their own goal within a 3-4-3 setup that lacked a true striker, opting instead for a ‘false’ one in Schmid. Every time they lost possession, it resulted in a counter-attack and often a goal.

It might seem odd to start with Frosinone rather than the brilliance of Milan, but there’s no denying that the visitors played their part in the spectacle. This is a match that future opponents will need to study in minute detail, because Milan on the counter are a goal-scoring machine.

Amorim, too, has a knack for springing surprises, though as always the guessing game regarding his actual tactical setup for the day begins the moment the whistle blows. For example, it was not a back four as it appeared on paper.

Instead, the system actually gradually morphed into a 3-5-2, with Rabiot operating as a highly advanced right-sided central midfielder, almost an attacking midfielder. The key lies in the connection between the Frenchman and the stratospheric Moreira, who surged down the centre often.

Keeping everything running at full throttle was the incredible playmaking of Modrić, who also serves as the team’s primary ball-winner. So much for being a ‘pensioner’.

Milan proved flawless in exploiting both structural weaknesses and individual errors. Frosinone’s DNA is defined by a headlong, aggressive approach, but the opening goal – stemming from a sequence on the right flank involving Modrić and Rabiot – ended up as an own goal by Calvani.

Just four minutes in, and the match was effectively decided. While Frosinone usually thrive on quick, darting attacks, here the roles were reversed. Another full-pitch surge, initiated by Ramos winning the ball from Calvani and carried forward by Moreira and Rabiot, left the Portuguese player unmarked to make it 2-0.

Only a reckless back pass from Musah gifted Masini a goal to pull it back to 2-1. In the second half, however, Amorim addressed the one area that looked shaky: he withdrew Bartesaghi – who had been struggling against Ghedjemis – shifting Musah to full-back and pairing Jashari with Modrić.

It paid off immediately: Jashari broke away and fired home the 3-1 following yet another rapid transition. And that wasn’t the only one: Pulisic surged clear on his own after a Frosinone corner (4-1), and Cissé, having just come on, joined the fray at full throttle to add the fifth (5-1).

There were many top performances. Rabiot is like a freight train and deserved a goal. He had to settle for three assists (bringing his total to seven). Moreira is versatile, playing as a wing-back, a central midfielder, or a winger, much like he did for Belgium when they caused Italy so much trouble.

Ramos also moved well outside of his goal. Cissé was an absolute handful: he came on and scorrd, playing as a striker after the Portuguese felt a tweak. He did so with an effortless grace that makes him impossible for his markers to handle.

The end result is that Milan are back in fourth. The competition is fierce, but the Rossoneri are right there in the mix, and eventually, some of the others will stumble. Take Inter, for example. Frosinone need to rethink their strategy while waiting for the return of Raimondo.

They’ve overachieved so far, but now they might need to be a bit more prudent. And what about Milan? If they don’t turn their trip to Athens into a Greek tragedy, perhaps their European campaign can get back on track, too.

#1513. Big Decision From Manchester United Captain As Pochettino Is Set To Take Over

Manchester United transfer news: Red Devils captain Bruno Fernandes has turned down a second contract offer, according to a report from The Athletic covered by CaughtOffside. The 32-year-old is unhappy with both the proposed salary and the length of the deal, and the standoff lands with his current contract set to expire in June 2027.

The calendar adds pressure. In 50 days, Fernandes can open talks with foreign clubs, and Galatasaray have already been linked. United hold a 12-month extension option that stops him leaving for free, but triggering it only postpones the argument and keeps an unhappy captain in the dressing room.

The refusal follows a bad few weeks. After a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes publicly criticised Michael Carrick’s tactics, and Carrick dropped him for the Bournemouth game. Carrick has since been sacked with United 18th in the Premier League, inside the relegation zone, so Mauricio Pochettino inherits the standoff alongside a team in trouble.

His strengths are obvious. He set a Premier League record with 21 assists last season, delivers set pieces better than anyone at the club and opened this campaign with a hat-trick against Ipswich. His weaknesses are just as clear. At 32, the Portuguese international gives little protection when United lose the ball, and his shot selection can be wasteful.

Pochettino’s best sides pressed hard and ran through a creative number ten with two athletic midfielders behind him. Fernandes suits the creative role, but only if those two midfielders cover his space.

United should keep him, but on shorter terms than he wants. Nobody else in the squad creates chances at his rate, and a team sitting in the bottom three cannot replace that in January. A long, expensive deal for a player entering his mid-thirties would create a wage problem just as Pochettino tries to rebuild the midfield around younger runners.

The sensible offer is a short contract with a raise tied to appearances and Champions League qualification. That respects his standing without committing United beyond the point where his legs start to fail.

If Fernandes still refuses, the board should trigger the extension and sell next summer. A sale with a year left on his deal will still bring a meaningful fee, whereas losing him for nothing in 2027 would waste the one asset United can sell on their own terms.

#1512. St Mirren boss McLeish claims 'self-interest' is hampering Scottish football development

Published: 09:55 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 09:55 EST, 20 November 2026

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish claims self-interest and poor governance are killing Scottish football’s hopes of improvement.

McLeish is frustrated that Scottish Football Association chief football officer Craig Mulholland has reportedly had to dilute plans for young player quotas to appease five William Hill Premiership clubs.

Mulholland was hoping to ensure teams featured Scotland Under-21 eligible players for an average of 60 minutes per league game and had two on the pitch for each cup tie.

McLeish said: 'That’s damning that he’s having to change his plans to pander to clubs who aren’t really on board with it and don’t really have the best interests of the Scottish national team at heart.

'I understand why. We have owners from outwith this country. We have managers from outwith this country. They’re in jobs, they’re all fighting for their clubs.

'But why then are those people allowed to be the ones that hold the keys to the future of our country and the development of our national team?

St Mirren boss Craig McLeish believes self-interest at clubs is hampering Scottish football

'It’s the way governance is set up and we’ve killed ourselves with that because the people who actually have a say in it have, not have no interest but they’ve got self-interest, and there’s a lot of self-interest at the top end.

'I just don’t see a way that we can really properly change unless something to do with governance changes and I just don’t ever see that happening. It’s really sad.'

Although McLeish backs quotas, he fears that would not address the root cause of Scottish football’s problems.

'We always focus at the top end, what our league size is, quotas for young players, a national base,' said the 36-year-old, who worked in St Mirren’s youth academy before his current role.

'We have a fundamental problem that starts at our youngest age groups, at four and five years of age, about how we actually teach kids to play. And until you fix that, you can’t fix the top end of it.

'It’s crazy some of the stuff that’s going on, the formats, how we teach kids. There’s just a massive lack of education and expertise at the very bottom of our pathway.

'In this country, football’s everyone’s sport and everyone gets access to it but if you take your young kids along to swimming or gymnastics or whatever other sport, you’re there with properly qualified coaches, teachers who have maybe done things at the top levels of that sport.

'We have nothing without the volunteers that work at the bottom end of the grassroots game, but they’re not teaching kids how to play football properly, in my mind.

'And you’re just hoping that they get put with a volunteer coach that can teach them something, that they get in with a really good group at the youngest ages.

'Because that development between the ages of three and eight, if you don’t get that right, you’re dead. You can’t do anything after that point, and we don’t do it well enough. And you’re just chasing yourself and we’ll never catch up.'

#1510. Chelsea Transfer News: Alonso Tells Right-Back To Leave

Chelsea transfer news: Xabi Alonso has reportedly told Malo Gusto to find a new club, according to CaughtOffside, who are citing Simon Phillips’ Substack. The report claims the 23-year-old France international does not suit the wing-back system Alonso has built at Stamford Bridge. It also floats a surprise swap that would send Gusto to Liverpool and reunite Alonso with Jeremie Frimpong, his former Bayer Leverkusen right wing-back.

Liverpool’s interest has history. They tried to sign Gusto on loan on deadline day, but Chelsea refused anything short of a permanent deal. Their right-back problem has run since Trent Alexander-Arnold left. Frimpong cost around £29.5million and has battled injuries and form, while Ronald Araujo is a centre-back covering on a season-long loan from Barcelona.

Gusto’s standing has slipped quickly. He started three of the first four league games, yet Josh Acheampong has since taken his place, and reports say he will be fourth choice behind Acheampong, Marco Palestra and Reece James once James returns from injury in early 2027.

His strength is defending, with 73 tackles and 36 chances created in 45 appearances last season. The weakness is end product, because three goals and five assists are modest for a wing-back who must supply Alonso’s right-hand width.

Frimpong supplies exactly that. The 25-year-old Dutchman scored 28 of his 30 Leverkusen goals under Alonso and thrives on pace and early crosses. Defending is his flaw, at 5ft 8in and with a poor injury record at Anfield.

No. Chelsea are fifth with 16 points from 10 games, but they have lost four, including 1-0 at Sunderland last Sunday and 3-0 at Brentford, and they concede too easily. Frimpong would add another attacker to a right side that already has James, Acheampong, Palestra and Pedro Neto, and he does nothing for a shaky back line. With no European football this season, Chelsea don’t need that many right-sided options anyway.

The money matters too. Both players have contracts until 2030 and similar valuations, so a straight swap brings Chelsea no cash and leaves Liverpool with their problem solved.

Sell Gusto instead, preferably abroad, since Paris Saint-Germain have been linked and Chelsea are reportedly open to cutting their asking price. Then spend that fee on a defensive midfielder or centre-back, because that is where Alonso’s team needs help.

#1509. Cisse discusses desire to add assists, not even being at 50% and why he must thank Gabbia

Alphadjo Cisse has revealed that he would like to add more assists to his game, as well as why he has Matteo Gabbia to thank above all.

Milan put on a ruthless display at San Siro on Sunday night, beating Frosinone 5-1 to move back into the top four. Calvani’s own-goal started the rout, while Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari and Christian Pulisic all scored.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Cisse got his name on the scoresheet again just minutes after coming on, netting his ninth goal of the season. Diego Moreira set him up with a nice through ball in transition, and though the offside flag went up initially, VAR overturned it to award the goal.

After the game, Cisse spoke to both Sky and DAZN to give his thoughts on what was another very positive night for him personally and for the team. His comments are via MilanNews.

“I definitely always try to contribute in all positions, and I definitely prefer to play in my own position, but I’m always available in all roles. Which position? I won’t say (laughs).”

Where can you still grow and what does Amorim ask of you?

“I have to improve in many other areas. As always, scoring is always great. I’d also like to add a few assists for some of my team-mates, but the most important thing was always to bring home three points, and today we did that.”

Is there a team-mate you have to thank in particular?

“I definitely think Gabbia, because I was initially coming from Serie B, and settling into that kind of environment is never easy. But I had teammates who welcomed me very well, him especially, so for me everything was much easier.”

We also see you as a possible centre-forward…

“I’ll tell you the truth, come on, I’ll tell you. I prefer to play in the attacking midfield because, as I’ve always done, I always want to try to make plays, to entertain people. But maybe, who knows, I’ll also play as a striker, I don’t know. Let’s see…”

“At first I thought it was. Then, as they were checking it a bit, I thought it wasn’t.”

You’re Milan’s top scorer. Will we see a bicycle kick soon?

“The overhead kick used to be my specialty, but now it’s not. Let’s hope it happens. It’s always a great feeling to score, I want to add a few assists too. The important thing was the three points, and we got them.”

How far along are you in your development?

“Right now, I’m not even halfway there. Maybe even lower. There’s still a lot of work to do to get there. But I’m in the right place, and hopefully we can get there.”

Have you ever thought about what would have happened if you had gone to PSV?

“Better not to think about it. Let’s just say that I’ve always made the right decisions with my family, and thanks go to them, to the coach, to my team-mates, and I’m in the right place and on the right path.”

“Progress is the right word, because we’ve changed coaches, and it’s never easy. We’re a great team, with many champions. We still have a lot of work to do. Milan always has our backs, and that’s very important to me.”

Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all contacted Bournemouth about England midfielder Alex Scott, according to CaughtOffside, which cites The i Paper. Liverpool and Chelsea want to move in January, while Arsenal would rather wait until next summer. Bournemouth’s stance on selling the 23-year-old has softened, but the reported asking price is above £100m, and Scott turned down two contract offers over the summer.

The interest has clear reasons behind it. Andoni Iraola coached Scott at Bournemouth before taking over at Anfield in June, and Liverpool want to reunite them. Chelsea lost Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City in a £125m deadline-day deal and had a reported £64m bid for Scott rejected earlier in the summer. Arsenal already have Declan Rice, Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Zubimendi and Myles Lewis-Skelly, so CaughtOffside sees Chelsea or Liverpool as the more logical destinations for his playing time.

Scott wins the ball, presses and carries it through midfield, and he started Bournemouth’s first five league games this season before a quadriceps injury on England duty in October kept him out for weeks. Fitness is the first concern, because knee problems have interrupted much of his time on the south coast. End product is the second. He has scored five league goals in 85 appearances since joining in 2023, so he will not solve a shortage of chances alone.

Not at £100m, and not as a January priority. Liverpool rank 18th for big chances after ten league games, according to This Is Anfield, and Scott offers energy rather than creativity. The real gap sits beside Ryan Gravenberch, where Curtis Jones left in the summer, and nobody arrived to share the defensive work.

Scott could be the aggressive partner in Iraola’s double pivot, freeing Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz to play higher, yet that is a heavy fee for a player only just rebuilding match fitness, with Liverpool fourth and nine points behind Arsenal.

Chelsea’s case is simpler. The division’s biggest summer spenders lost their midfield engine and can justify the price more easily. Arsenal’s patience makes sense, since Rice, Guimaraes and Zubimendi leave no room for a £100m squad player. A Liverpool bid would only inflate the market Chelsea are already shaping. If Iraola wants a January signing, a specialist holding midfielder for far less money does more for the top-four push.

#1506. Liverpool Transfer News: Dutch Star’s Agent Tests Market

Liverpool transfer news: Ryan Gravenberch’s agent, José Fortes Rodriguez, is exploring ways to take his client out of Anfield, according to CaughtOffside. The site relays a claim from the X account @ITKSpace that Fortes has held “loose but direct contact” with several European clubs, none of them named. No formal exit request has been lodged, and the 24-year-old could still stay, so this reads like a camp checking the market rather than a player pushing to leave.

Liverpool hold the stronger hand. His six-year extension, signed in March, runs to 2032, so any buyer would face a substantial asking price. Real Madrid have been linked before, though nothing here says they are interested now.

Iraola’s 4-2-3-1 relies on two central midfielders, and Gravenberch, so commanding at the base of Arne Slot’s title-winning side, has struggled to settle. Iraola benched him for three straight games at one stage, he collected a second yellow card in the 3-0 home defeat by Manchester City on 11 October, and a heel problem has since kept him out of the Arsenal and Fenerbahçe games. He has no goals and one assist in the league this term.

His strengths are clear. At 6ft 3in he carries the ball through pressure and starts attacks from deep. Defending space and tracking runners is the weakness, and it shows when his partner also surges forward.

No, not this winter and not at a price set by his worst few weeks. Gravenberch is 24, tied down until 2032, and his market value has slipped sharply since last December, so selling now would hand a buyer the bargain that March contract was meant to rule out.

The real problem sits elsewhere. Iraola received no new midfielder in the summer, and his double pivot has no natural holding player. Gravenberch has admitted he prefers the number eight role, yet Mac Allister and Szoboszlai, who started the 3-1 win at Crystal Palace that lifted Liverpool to fourth, already occupy those spots. Nineteen-year-old Trey Nyoni has mostly played the deeper role this season.

Keep him through January, get him fit, and judge him again in a settled pairing. If Liverpool then sign a proper holding midfielder next summer, Gravenberch becomes a surplus eight, and a big-club bid at the right figure would deserve a hearing. Selling before that signing arrives just removes the one midfielder who can still carry the ball out of pressure.

#1505. Villa Midfielder Has £80m Price Tag For Arsenal: Is He Worth It?

Arsenal transfer news: Aston Villa do not regard Boubacar Kamara as available, even with Arsenal interested, according to CaughtOffside. The report says an offer of around £80m could change that stance, although Villa negotiate from strength because the 26-year-old’s contract runs until 2030.

January looks highly unlikely. Villa have already lost Amadou Onana to a torn ACL suffered at the World Cup, and the Belgian is not expected back until around April. Unai Emery cannot lose a second holding midfielder in the middle of a season. The summer is different. CaughtOffside says Villa could entertain a significant bid then, provided they can reinvest the money in a proper replacement and strengthen the squad around him.

TBR Football reported in July 2025 that he sat on Arsenal’s long list of midfield targets, and his numbers explain why. Kamara has started all 10 of his Premier League games this season, completing 86.3% of his passes, including 83 line-breaking balls, while making 28 tackles and 40 recoveries. He wins 56% of his duels and can play at centre-back, which would give Mikel Arteta cover in two positions.

The weaknesses are just as clear. He has no goals this season, only three shots and an xG of 0.14, and he has committed 20 fouls and conceded a penalty. He also missed the closing weeks of 2024/25 through injury.

The role he would play is obvious: a ball-playing six next to Declan Rice. Martín Zubimendi occupies it now, and Arsenal lead the league with 27 points from 10 games, six clear of Manchester City, with seven clean sheets.

No, not at that price. Arsenal spent £75m on Bruno Guimarães in August, and Arteta still has Rice, Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Martin Ødegaard and Myles Lewis-Skelly competing for the same central spaces.

FotMob values him at €49m, roughly £43m, so Villa would be asking close to double his market value for a player who turns 27 this month and offers little in the final third. Villa’s insistence on reinvesting the fee also hands them the leverage, which means Arsenal would pay a premium on a seller’s timetable.

The only sensible trigger is a departure, perhaps Zubimendi or the 30-year-old Merino, leaving Arsenal short of a proven Premier League six. Kamara is a better holding midfielder than most of the market, but a title-leading side already has that job covered, and £80m would buy cover rather than improvement.

#1504. Chelsea’s £43m Winger Gamble Is Stalling: Should They Accept A Discount?

Chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met. Chelsea sent the 22-year-old to Villa Park on a season-long loan in July, with a reported £43m obligation to buy next summer. Neither club has revealed the trigger, and reports link it to appearances.

The numbers explain the concern. FotMob lists four Premier League outings, all from the bench, without a goal or assist, while Football365 counts only 95 minutes across seven substitute appearances. Football Insider claims Villa are prepared to back out of the deal if his form doesn’t improve.

Garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed. His pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders earned a £40m move from Manchester United in 2025. The weakness is end product, and it followed him to London with eight goals in 43 games for Chelsea, only one of them in 24 Premier League appearances. Unai Emery left him out of the squad for the Manchester United game.

Chelsea have no obvious use for him either. Xabi Alonso told him in July that regular football wasn’t guaranteed, and the 3-4-2-1 Alonso favours uses Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer behind João Pedro, with Pedro Neto and Estêvão competing for the wide roles.

FotMob values him at about €29m (roughly £25m), far below the €71m peak recorded in August 2024, and Manchester United are reportedly entitled to 10 per cent of any future fee. If the clause isn’t triggered, he returns in July 2027 on a contract running to 2032.

Yes, and soon. Chelsea built the deal to protect £43m, but the clause relies on appearances from a manager who isn’t picking him, so the price drops with every unused substitution. The sporting case for a return is thin. Alonso’s system asks wide players to defend as wing-backs, while Garnacho’s value lies in isolating a full-back, and the £117m Rogers signing already covers the left-sided attacking role.

A mid-£20m sale, even after United’s cut, would still return more than half of the £40m Chelsea paid and clear a contract running to 2032. Chelsea should open talks with Villa in January about a lower fixed fee, or line up other buyers for the summer. A clause that depends on a manager picking a player he has benched was never a safe way to protect £43m.

#1503. How Mykhailo Mudryk's unsolicited interview turned into a moany mess: With gaffes galore - including his Arsenal 'dream' - the £89m man hasn't endeared himself to either Spurs or Chelsea, writes KIERAN GILL

Published: 07:05 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:02 EST, 20 November 2026

Not for the first time, Mykhailo Mudryk was in a good position, and displayed poor judgement. This time, it was away from the pitch, in a two-hour, sit-down, tell-all interview involving gaffes galore.

Criticising London for its 20mph speed limit, saying 'it's hard to follow these rules, however much I'd like to' after his latest driving ban, and how the wealthy are taxed 45 per cent on these shores.

Naming 'Ukraine' when asked which is the best city in the world – he may have misunderstood the question, so we will let him off with that one – and admitting he signed contracts without reading them while denouncing the deals done by his former representatives.

Then there was his interviewer, a grinning chap called Dmitry Gordon, asking him if he speaks to his four cats in English, and why he wears earrings, and if girls send him pictures. Bizarre enquiries. Had Chelsea or Tottenham Hotspur known about this interview happening – and Daily Mail Sport understands they were not informed – then we cannot imagine either Premier League club would have liked such lines of questioning.

Nor will they, or their fanbases, be too fond of the 25-year-old Ukrainian explaining his move to England in the first place. He revealed how much he wanted to play for Arsenal, describing it as his 'dream' as he blamed his old agent for pushing him to Chelsea for the money.

What was supposed to be an opportunity for Mudryk to tell his side of the story, after a doping ban which cost him two years of his career, resembled more of a moany mess.

Mykhailo Mudryk's interview was a bizarre mess and showed his utter naivety

The Ukrainian winger was given a one-year driving ban in December last year

By the end, the seriousness of his allegations against the Ukrainian national team with regard to his failed drugs test were softened by the nonsensical own goals much more likely to set social media alight.

Such as the naivety of a Chelsea player on loan at Tottenham appearing to pine for Arsenal, and saying he still wants to win the Ballon d'Or, which is only ever an admission prone to being patronised online even if a sign of his ambition.

A reminder: Mudryk signed for Chelsea from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023 for £89million. He struggled, never looked like a winger worth such a fee. Frighteningly fast, but did not know how to use his weaponry properly in the Premier League. Graham Potter was his manager when he arrived. A few months later, it was Frank Lampard. A month after that, Mauricio Pochettino.

Then he was suspended for two years, during which time Chelsea supported his insistence that he was innocent and continued to pay his salary, believed to be worth around £100,000 per week.

While banned, he turned up in Wroclaw, Poland the day before the 2025 Conference League final, apparently there to collect his medal in case Chelsea won. Enzo Maresca was unaware, only learning that he was in the city when we told him at his pre-match press conference.

Upon Mudryk's return to football in the summer of 2026, Chelsea decided he needed to leave on loan, and another one of the Premier League's big-six sides gave him his second chance.

Tottenham called. Brentford, Brighton, Leeds and Coventry were among those also willing, but Roberto De Zerbi promised to give him a platform to prove his talents.

He appeared once, as a 74th-minute substitute away at Nottingham Forest in September. Then he disappeared, injured, and his only sighting since has been here, on YouTube, as a 'Guest of Gordon'.

Chelsea will also be unhappy about Mudryk's interview and were not informed about it

Mykhailo Mudryk's is still two weeks away from a Tottenham return after a suffering setback to his recovery from an ankle injury.

Mudryk, who has played only 16 minutes since joining on loan from Chelsea, clashed with the Ukrainian FA this week when he blamed them for his positive drug test which ruled him out of football for almost two years.

He also risked the wrath of Spurs fans by admitting he only made the move across London to recover his fitness before returning to Stamford Bridge where Blues boss Xabi Alonso was 'counting on him'.

And he managed to annoy both Chelsea and Spurs fans by revealing, during the same YouTube interview, that he wanted to sign for Arsenal when he moved to the Premier League in January 2023 but his agent forced through the move with the best commission.

'I can understand the fans, but Mudryk is a good guy,' said Spurs boss De Zerbi, who worked with the Ukraine international at Shakhtar Dontetsk and convinced him to resist interest from Brentford and Coventry and be reunited in North London.

'He's a good player. He suffered a lot for the situation in the last couple of years. He has just one thing to do, show on the pitch his qualities, show on the pitch that now he's playing for Tottenham. Tottenham is a big club, like the other clubs, not less at all.'

Chelsea paid £86million for Mudryk but he made little impression before he was hit with a four-year ban in 2024, which was wiped out this summer enabling him to return to competition.

'He has no responsibility in this part,' said De Zerbi. 'Now his focus is just on the ball or just on the football. He has a big chance to play with us because Tottenham is a big club. He knows very well the coach, he knows very well the style of play.

'He knows I give him total confidence to show what he is. So to move the focus in the right direction, in a good direction. But I think he's working hard to recover and to play earlier.'

Mudryk made his Spurs debut as a sub at Nottingham Forest in September but injured an ankle in training a few days later. He was initially expected to be out for two months with Saturday's game against Ipswich his target to return.

'The plan was to be available for Ipswich or Sunderland,' said De Zerbi, who will serve a touchline ban against Ipswich for three yellow cards. 'Then he felt not pain but he was not comfortable last week. And they take two weeks more, and step by step we're going to see the situation.'

While there should be sympathy with Mudryk, who had to bite his tongue while banned and spending what he described as 'millions' on trying to clear his name, he made a poor choice in the platform chosen to finally speak up.

At one stage, he is asked bluntly whether he considered killing himself. 'No, that's not a way out,' he replied. The title of the video on YouTube, unhelpfully, mentions 'suicidal thoughts' regardless of his answer.

Mudryk may have thought it would help to talk so openly, especially to clarify those he holds responsible for the two years he lost as a footballer.

But he hardly endeared himself to his current club, Tottenham, or to his parent club, Chelsea, to whom he is still contracted into the 2030s.

He likened them to chaos, explaining: 'I came to a Chelsea that was, and perhaps still is, in the middle of a rebuild. It's not the Chelsea that existed under the previous owners, which was stable, had a clear system, coaches, without this constant galloping who knows where.'

Such comments are unlikely to be well received when read by the club's hierarchy, while he also said on Chelsea's managerial merry-go-round: 'The coaches themselves don't know what tactics they'll play. They come to the club and try one set of tactics. Whether it works or not, they try another.'

When Mudryk returns from his ankle injury, he will have to hope his football can do the talking. After this, neither Tottenham nor Chelsea are likely to want him to speak again any time soon.

#1502. Liverpool Open Talks With Argentine Midfielder: Is He Worth A New Deal?

Liverpool transfer news: Liverpool have opened contract talks with Alexis Mac Allister, according to @tribuna_ftbl, with his current deal running until June 2028. The report arrives days after his father, Carlos, told ESPN that no discussions had started, although he hinted at news before the end of the year.

It also reverses the summer, when the club extended Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai but made no offer to the 27-year-old, something Mac Allister revealed in September while admitting he had stayed despite chances to leave.

His form explains the change. After a poor 2025/26 under Arne Slot, he has become Andoni Iraola’s first-choice midfielder alongside Szoboszlai, pushing Gravenberch to the bench. He has scored once in the Premier League and three times in the Champions League, including the winner against Atlético Madrid, and holds a 7.29 FotMob average rating across 758 league minutes. Liverpool sit fourth.

FotMob places him in the 88th percentile among midfielders for shot attempts, and he has said the man-to-man system suits him because it demands less communication than Slot’s approach. His weaknesses are just as clear.

His defensive contributions (45th percentile) and aerial duels (46th) sit below the midfield average, and pundit David Lynch has questioned whether his legs have gone in Iraola’s 4-4-2, where two central midfielders cover huge areas. He has also collected four league yellow cards already.

Yes, but not on the terms his summer rebound might demand. Ten league games of good form do not cancel a season in which he looked off the pace, so Liverpool should offer around three years, with wages pitched below the bumper deals Gravenberch and Szoboszlai signed.

The timing still makes sense. With 18 months left, he enters the final year next summer, when Liverpool would face either a discounted sale or a free departure. His FotMob valuation of €66m has almost halved from the €130m peak of September 2025, so selling now would lock in the lowest price.

Iraola also needs a controller to sit beside Szoboszlai’s runs, and no one in the squad does that better. The caveat is that Mac Allister turns 28 next month, so Liverpool must pair him with a quicker partner next summer rather than treat his renewal as the end of the midfield rebuild.

#1501. Real Madrid vs. PSV Eindhoven: Jose Mourinho makes Vinicius Junior promise amid superstar's struggles

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 18:01, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 18:02

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has insisted that struggling Brazilian superstar Vinicius Junior will "return to his full potential".

The 26-year-old signed a new mega-money deal with Real Madrid over the summer after rejecting the chance to make the move to Arsenal.

However, it has been a tough campaign for the attacker, who has only come up with one goal and three assists in 13 appearances for the club.

Vinicius was left out of the starting XI against Celta Vigo in the league on Saturday, instead featuring as a second-half substitute in his side's 2-1 success.

Mourinho has confirmed that the forward will be involved in Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV Eindhoven, and the Portuguese remains convinced that the South American will soon return to his highest level for Los Blancos.

“He’ll return to his full potential. He’s young, and sometimes when players approach or pass the age of 30, they struggle to maintain their ideal physical condition and some lose a bit of their motivation," Mourinho told reporters during Monday's press conference.

"Vini Jr. is young, and people can forget that he arrived very young and reached an extremely high level far too soon. He’s won everything, but when people were out to get him, he always said he’s a really good lad and very empathetic towards everyone.

"That’s a fundamental foundation. He had a very positive impact the other day and I remember that against Villarreal he turned the game around, but he was out for four matches due to his sending-off and that disrupted his development and his confidence. At the weekend he came on well and helped turn the match around.

“He’s playing tomorrow and we’re all hoping to see him at his best. I saw him last season, but on the other side, with Benfica dominating and the Bernabeu silent. A goal from Vini Jr. and the tie was over.

"That’s the Vini Jr. we want, but as far as I’m concerned there’s no pressure – he just needs to keep working hard as he’s been doing and help the team in attack and with defensive organisation. If he gives his all alongside me, he doesn’t need to be the man of the match.”

Vinicius has been named in the squad for Real Madrid's European clash with PSV on Tuesday, but Endrick, Rodrygo, Raul Asencio and Ferland Mendy are out due to injuries.

Denzel Dumfries missed training on Monday and was regarded as a doubt, but the Netherlands international has been named in the squad.

#1500. Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

“I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

Grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

As Dominic says, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

If you largely try and defend a 1-0 lead and don’t go for that second goal, there’s always the danger of that happening. Superb finish from George to equalise but it’s been so passive from United. Asking for trouble and they’ve got it. Big 7 minutes plus injury time for them now.

Free-kick on the left, parallel with the penalty spot. Hackney bends it in with his right and Branthwaite heads it on target but too close to Lammens who oddly elects to punch.

Mykolenko gives the ball back from the throw-in as Fernandes serves his minute on the sidelines.

Dalot is booked for pulling Grealish’s shirt when the left winger had spun him.

Maitland-Niles receives a warm reception. I had forgotten that he has five England caps.

Bruno Fernandes goes down after kicking Tarkowski’s studs when his foot was raised. The referee does not stop play but books Maguire for complaining when the ball eventually goes out.

Garner almost immediately goes down and starts stretching his calves.

Mykolenko hurls a long throw into the Man Utd box. Dewsbury-Hall meets it with a shot that he catches sweetly but hits a defender. The ball rebounds to Armstrong who scuffs his attempt wide .

George has switched to the right to accommodate Grealish. I wonder if there was ever a possibility of him returning to Villa? Would Unai Emery treasure him?

“He’s back!” the stadium announcer has proclaimed, as Jack Grealish has entered the fray. The move has provided an immediate bounce but let’s see what the former England man can do to change the pattern of the game. Everton believe they have got a £100m player. It’s time to show it.

Grealish’s first contribution sends Mykolenko away on an overlap and Martinez messes up his clearance from the cross, shanking it behind for a corner that they defend soundly.

Manchester United corner on the left after Tielemans’ 25-yard shot was deflected behind. Fernandes plays it along the ground to Shaw in the D. The left-back’s control spoons the ball up with his left so he improvises a right-foot volley with his swinger, dragging it predictably wide.

Rohl is beaten yet again by Rashford and works his way into the book after pulling him back. It’s been hard going for the Everton right back against Rashford but United just haven’t taken advantage of it enough.

Jack Grealish is stripped and ready to come on.

Rashford jinks at pace 35 yards up the inside-left channel, chopping to the left and barrelling between defenders. He takes it too wide to shoot so cutely backheels to Cunha who pulls back his left foot to shoot from six yards but Tarkowski slides his leg through his gait and pokes the ball away. The away fans shout for a penalty but Cunha has no complaints.

Barry diddles Martinez by feinting to the right and then darting left to open a rout to goal. He hammers a shot from about 16 yards that Shaw slides across to block, diverting it to Dewsbury-Hall whose follow-up effort is a tame daisycutter that Lammens easily gathers.

It threatened to be the case that a Manchester United goal would puncture the atmosphere completely and so it has proven. The likelihood here is the away team will score again in the next 10 minutes to completely kill the game. Everton have endured a miserable week and this flat performance is entirely in keeping with the narrative.

Johnson cuts in off the right to run on to Garner’s pass and shoots from 18 yards. Martinez makes himself as big as possible and the shot clips his calf, sending it up before it dips threateningly, whistling over the bar.

Mbeumo heads out Garner’s corner. Dewsbury-Hall crosses it back into the box and Tarkowski tries to head it across into the middle. Manchester United clear their lines.

Shaw slides in to block Dewsbury-Hall’s shot after the attacking midfielder had manipulated an opportunity with a quick interchange with Johnson.

Key for Manchester United, who have taken the lead in a match for the first time this season, not to let up on the tempo with which they started this half.

Everton respond with a menacing cross in from the left, from George, I think, that eludes Johnson as he arrives in the middle a second late.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh

We hadn’t seen that Mbeumo in the first half – so much better, driving inside at pace and with intent. Good decoy run from Fernandes. Top finish from Mbeumo.

Both managers will want to see a lot more urgency from their sides in the second half. Rashford has been United’s most threatening outlet and has the beating of Rohl but Mbeumo and Cunha were poor in those opening 45 minutes and both guilty of turning over the ball cheaply when United were breaking late in the first period. Barry should have hit the target with a header from Rohl’s cross. But it’s been a lacklustre game, low in quality so far.

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Everton look wide open on the right side of their defence and Brennan Johnson is starting to make headway against Luke Shaw.

Brilliant sliding tackle from Branthwaite when Rashford, piling down the inside-left channel in full flight. Just as he was about to pull the trigger, Branthwaite launched himself to knock it away and leapt back to his feet to block Fernandes’ stinging follow-up with the his head.

Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

There will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Rohl and Barry link up in more orthodox fashion with an excellent, dipping cross from the right-back. Barry peels off Maguire and thumps his header wide. That’s the best chance of the game.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

Everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

It was Johnson who was under scrutiny for a ‘foul’ on Martinez’ but it was just a hand on the back.

Branthwaite is winded when he collides with Pickford in midair defending a back-post cross. Seems to be OK.

Fernandes whips over a cross and Armstrong beats Martínez to head it clear. VAR is looking at Martínez’s claim that he was fouled. Now it’s been cleared.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

Shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

Ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

Best move of the game to date should have ended with Cunha hitting the target. The silkiest bit about it was how Rashford lulled Rohl into a false sense of security with his first touch then tapped the ball past him in the next movement just as Rohl was engaging. Very clever.

Now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

Dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

Dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Big shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

Slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? When they play away at Everton, their kit has always been – and always should be – red shirts, black shorts and black socks. It looks odd with two teams playing in white shorts. This may seem a random observation but there we go... there hasn’t been any action to discuss in the opening four minutes!

Maguire returns to the fray as Everton pass the ball through midfield to Johnson on the right. His cross, aiming for Barry, is cut out by Maguire and cleared to halfway. Back come Everton until Dewsbury-Hall is too rough with Mainoo as the Man Utd midfielder tackled him. Free-kick.

Lammens kicks the ball the full length of the field and Pickford picks it up. Mbeumo momentarily is at right-back with Dalot at centre-half.

Maguire is OK to continue but he will be off the field for the mandatory minute.

Maguire headed the back of Barry’s head and splattered his nose. He should be all right though he might need the cotton wool nostril bungs for a while, like Blackadder, the pencils and ‘wibble’.

Big cheers goes around the stadium when Harrison Armstrong’s name has read out. Everton would likely have sold him had there not been a backlash from fans opposing his sale.

Concern here for Harry Maguire. Looks in distress on the ground, laying very still. Concerned players around.

Leny Yoro is warming up on the touchline.

Looks like he caught the back of Barry’s head as he went to challenge. Sat up nose receiving treatment on a very bloodied nose.

Everton kick off, attacking from right to left. The fans, as usual, are making a racket. Everton work the ball back to Pickford who clips a diagonal up the left. Everton play it towards Barry who collides with Maguire who takes a blow to the head.

The teams emerge from the tunnel, both teams in their home kits with the only twist Manchester United’s switch to white socks.

We’re looking forward to seeing what [Brennan Johnson] does. We know he is very capable [and shown it] in recent seasons. Let’s hope he can bring us goals and assists as he did for Tottenham.

We’ve needed them [the two deadline day signings]. Maitland-Niles is physically fine. I don’t think Jack should be yet. We’ve needed it.

That’s all gone now [deadline day]. It’s all about the football. That’s what people are coming to see and we’ll have to play as well as we have done in our opening two games, get a positive result. Hopefully we can continue to build on it.

Nothing different [expected from the fans today]. They’re always really good for us.

No surprise United remain unchanged from the 5-2 win over Ipswich although Carrick will be looking for his side to score first here and make life a little easier for themselves after going behind to Hull and Ipswich in their opening two games. Brennan Johnson comes in for the departed Iliman Ndiaye, who joined Manchester City for £65m on deadline day. Jack Grealish is on the bench for Everton.

Moyes issued a call to arms to Everton fans in his programme notes after a dismal transfer window that has left him with just 18 outfield players. The Everton manager warning there may be difficult times to come.

“Finally, I must stress the importance of us all pulling together,” Moyes wrote.

“We need to be strong again and there may be occasions when we may have to find a way to get through some difficult moments.

“It is something you have all done in recent seasons. Everyone has pulled together for the good of the football club and we may need to do so again.”

We did a lot of good things [against Ipswich]. No two games are ever the same. We have different challenges today. We have to be ready for that with some slightly different ideas. But the boys did well last week, trained well this week and we’re really looking forward to it.

The next result is always the most important one regardless of what’s happened. Building momentum, building a run, of course it’s important. It’s game-by-game, as you know, but this is as tough as it comes for us, Everton away.

It’s not a major deal, we’ve got the squad and we can cope with it [increase in numbers of fixtures with the return to European football].

Everton  Pickford; Röhl, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry. Substitutes Travers, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Grealish, O’Brien, Dibling, Alcaraz, Hackney, Graham.

Man Utd  Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martínez, Shaw; Tielemans, Mainoo; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford; Cunha. Substitutes Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.
